the_closure: The functional-navigation program is closed. Where a free subspace exists it is not integrable; where motion is integrable it is not free; and wherever the OOD gradient is available at all, joint training on the combined data beats navigating. Combined with DISCOVERY-009, which showed no training-only signal identifies the useful direction, there is no configuration in which navigation is both possible and useful.

the_surviving_result.derivation: rank(J_train) = min(n, P - g) since the gauge kernel is structural and shared by every distribution. dim ker(J_train) = P - rank. Removing the g gauge directions, which are inert for every distribution, leaves max(0, P - g - n).
the_surviving_result.explanatory_power: This is why every navigation attempt in DISCOVERY-007 through 009 failed. Those ran at n=600 with P-g=193, so d_free = 0 exactly. There was no free subspace to find, and the searches were structurally doomed rather than unlucky.
the_surviving_result.novelty: Elementary rank-nullity plus an identified gauge dimension. No novelty is claimed. Its value is that it converts a string of empirical failures into a predicted consequence.
the_surviving_result.statement: Let P be the parameter count, g the structural gauge dimension (softmax common mode, g = h + 1 for h hidden units and 2 classes), and n the number of training points. The first-order subspace of directions that preserve all training predictions while being able to change predictions elsewhere has dimension d_free = max(0, P - g - n).
the_surviving_result.status: Stated BEFORE measurement, then confirmed exactly.

title: Closure of the functional-navigation program, with the dimension law that explains it
verdict: NAVIGATION PROGRAM CLOSED. One exact derived result survives and it is the explanation for the closure.
what_the_program_should_take_from_this: Three separate mechanisms were required to close this, and each is a reusable control: check d_free before searching for free directions; check integrability before trusting a first-order subspace; and check whether the simplest use of the same information already dominates.

why_the_free_regime_does_not_rescue_navi.control_1_non_integrability: ker(J_train) is a first-order object. Train logit displacement grows essentially linearly with arc length: 7.3e-5, 7.3e-3, 1.78e-1, 2.26, 1.46e1 at arcs 0.01, 0.1, 0.5, 2.0, 7.5. At any step large enough to matter the trajectory has left the kernel, so 'zero-cost navigation' does not survive finite motion.
why_the_free_regime_does_not_rescue_navi.control_2_projection_adds_nothing: At n=100 and matched arc, kernel-projected motion gives dOOD +0.0525 and held-out +0.0267 for dL 2.12e-2, while plain OOD gradient gives dOOD +0.0583 and held-out +0.0347 for dL 4.10e-2. The projection halves the training damage but also reduces the OOD gain, and loses outright on held-out OOD. It is a mild tradeoff, not a win.
why_the_free_regime_does_not_rescue_navi.control_3_fatal: The apparent free-regime gain is simply the use of OOD labels. Training jointly on train plus OOD from scratch DOMINATES every navigation variant on every axis at once: dL 1.86e-2 (lowest), test 0.9845 (highest), dOOD +0.0758 (highest), held-out OOD +0.0423 (highest). The simplest possible use of the same information beats all the machinery.
